overview.subtitle: The foundation of every management system: what affects the organisation, who has requirements of it, what the management system covers, and how leadership steers through policies and clear responsibilities.

setup.title: Get started
setup.intro: Take these steps in order. Each one builds on the one before, and the list disappears once everything is in place.

todo.context_analysis: What affects the organisation from inside and outside?
todo.interested_party: Who has requirements and expectations of you?
todo.scope_statement: What does the management system cover, and what is outside it?
todo.responsibility: Who does what, and who is accountable?

overview.addScopeFor: Add a scope statement for {{ framework }}
overview.allScoped: Every standard the organisation follows has an approved scope.
overview.allPolicies: Every expected policy type has an approved policy.

attention.partiesNotAddressed: Interested parties whose needs are not addressed
attention.segregation: Responsibilities where the same person does and approves the work
attention.analysesWithoutFollowUp: Context analyses with weaknesses or threats not followed up
attention.policiesNotCommunicated: Approved policies nobody has been asked to read
attention.none: Nothing else is waiting. Well done!

matrix.title: RACI matrix
matrix.body: See every responsibility on one page: who does the work, who is accountable, and who actually holds each role today.

pack.title: Evidence for the audit
pack.body: Download the scope, policies, RACI, interested parties and context analyses with their approval trail, ready for the certification body.
pack.failed: Could not create the evidence pack. Try again in a moment.

descriptions.analysis: SWOT and PESTEL analyses of the issues that affect the organisation.
descriptions.party: Who has requirements and expectations of the organisation, and how you follow them up.
descriptions.scope: What each management system covers, and which requirements do not apply.
descriptions.policy: Leadership's commitments, approved and communicated to staff.
descriptions.responsibility: Who is responsible for, accountable for, consulted on and informed about each duty.

fields.title: Title
fields.name: Name
fields.isComplianceObligation: Some of these requirements are legal or other obligations the organisation must meet

categoryHints.strength: Internal: what the organisation does well and can build on.
categoryHints.weakness: Internal: where the organisation falls short or is vulnerable.
categoryHints.opportunity: External: changes the organisation can benefit from.
categoryHints.threat: External: changes that could harm the organisation.
categoryHints.economic: Markets, prices, interest rates, labour supply.
categoryHints.legal: Laws, regulations and agreements that apply.

priorityHints.manage_closely: High influence and high interest: involve them actively and keep them close.
priorityHints.keep_satisfied: High influence, lower interest: make sure their requirements are met.
priorityHints.keep_informed: High interest, lower influence: keep them up to date.
priorityHints.monitor: Lower influence and interest: watch for changes.

analysis.boardHint: Turn weaknesses and threats into risks, and strengths and opportunities into objectives. That ties the context analysis to your risk work and your objectives.
analysis.followUpFailed: The record was saved and linked to the analysis, but not to the factor itself. Link it from the analysis.

party.obligationHint: Legal and contractual requirements from this party should be recorded as obligations of their own, so they are followed up and evidenced (ISO 14001 and ISO 45001 clause 6.1.3).

registers.title: Linked to the registers
registers.none: Not linked to any records yet.

hint.customer: Link the contracts and customer feedback from these customers.
hint.employee: Link employees and positions in the people register.
hint.owner: Link the agreements with the owners.
hint.regulator: Link the legal requirements and obligations this authority stands behind.
hint.supplier: Link the suppliers and contracts this concerns.
hint.partner: Link the agreements with the partners.
hint.community: Link the records that show how the organisation follows up its neighbours and community.
hint.competitor: Link the risks and opportunities that concern competitors.
hint.other: Link the records that show how the organisation follows up this party.

scope.noExclusions: No requirements are excluded. Every requirement of the standard applies.
scope.exclusionsHint: While the scope is approved, these requirements count as not applicable in the requirement coverage.
scope.exclusionsFormHint: Choose the clause of the standard, and explain why it does not apply to the organisation.
scope.addExclusion: Add a requirement that does not apply
scope.soaMissing: The ISO/IEC 27001 scope refers to the Statement of Applicability, but the organisation does not have one yet.

policy.noDocuments: No policy document is linked yet.
policy.documentLinked: {{ name }} is linked to the policy.
policy.documentPlaceholder: Search documents by title or code
policy.documentHint: The controlled document with the approved policy text. This is what staff read.
policy.objectivesHint: The policy should provide the framework for the objectives the organisation sets.
policy.noObjectives: No objectives have been set from this policy yet.
policy.available: Yes, can be shared with interested parties

ack.title: Communicated and confirmed
ack.breakdown: {{ pending }} waiting, {{ overdue }} past the due date.
ack.empty: Nobody has been asked to confirm this version yet.
ack.none: Nobody has been asked to read and confirm this version yet.

raci.matrixDescription: Every responsibility on one page, with who holds each role today.
raci.matrixCaption: Responsibilities (rows) per role, department or person (columns)
raci.matrixEmpty: Add responsibilities to build the matrix.
raci.columnCountsLabel: Responsible in {{ r }}, accountable in {{ a }}, consulted in {{ c }}, informed in {{ i }}

warningSummary.segregation_of_duties: Same person does and approves: {{ count }}
warningSummary.no_members: Roles or departments without people: {{ count }}

raci.legend: R does the work, A is accountable for the result (exactly one), C is consulted beforehand, I is informed afterwards.
raci.add: Add a person, role or department
raci.addHint: Pick someone to add them to this responsibility.

warningText.no_accountable: Nobody is accountable for the result (A). Choose exactly one.
warningText.no_responsible: Nobody is responsible (R). Choose who does the work.
warningText.segregation_of_duties: The same person both does the work and approves it. Split the duties between two people, or describe how it is checked.

approve.title: Approve
approve.message: Approve “{{ title }}”. It becomes the current approved version.
approve.label: Comment (optional)

return.title: Return to draft
return.message: Return “{{ title }}” to draft. Say what needs to change.
return.label: Reason

review.title: Mark as reviewed
review.message: Confirm that “{{ title }}” has been reviewed and still applies. The next review moves by the review interval.
review.label: Review notes (optional)

retire.title: Retire
retire.message: Retire “{{ title }}”. It stays in the history but can no longer be edited.
retire.label: Reason (optional)

delete.title: Delete {{ type }}?
delete.message: Delete “{{ title }}”? Open tasks are cancelled. The activity trail is kept.

detail.notFound: The item does not exist, or you do not have access to it.
detail.approvedNote: Changing the content starts a new version that must be approved.

form.ownershipHint: The owner keeps the content up to date and is reminded when a review is due.
form.requiredLegend: Fields with a star must be filled in.
form.nextHint: Choose how often, and the next review is set for you. You can also pick a date yourself.
form.nextComputed: The next review is set to {{ date }} from the interval. You can change the date.
form.frameworksHint: Choose the management systems this applies to. It then documents the matching requirement in each of those standards automatically.
form.processPlaceholder: Search processes by name or code

hints.requirements: Describe the requirements in your own words. Record laws and agreements as obligations.
hints.obligation: Tick this when the party sets requirements the organisation must meet, such as laws, permits or agreements.
hints.monitoring: For example a yearly customer survey, meetings with union representatives, or legal update alerts.
hints.processes: Choose the processes in scope. They also show on the processes' own pages.
hints.policyStatement: Write what leadership commits to. The policy must suit the purpose, frame the objectives and commit to meeting requirements and improving.
hints.available: Tick this when the policy may be given to customers, authorities and other interested parties.
hints.process: Choose the process from the process register. If it is not there, enter an area below.
hints.area: Use this when the responsibility does not belong to one process.

form.archived: Archived (kept as evidence, hidden from active lists)
form.approvedNotice: You are editing an approved version. Changing the content starts a new draft version that must be approved again. Changing only the owner, the review or the policy document does not.
form.reasonRequired: Required: why is the approved content changing?
form.reasonOptional: Optional: why are you changing this?
form.cannotSave: Could not save. Fix this first:

problems.title: Fill in the title.
problems.name: Fill in the name.
problems.framework: Choose which standard the scope is for.
problems.interval: Choose a review interval from the list.
problems.exclusion: Each requirement that does not apply needs both a clause and a reason.

communicate.title: Communicate the policy
communicate.intro: Ask people to read and confirm the policy. Each person gets their own task in My work, and the policy shows who has confirmed.
communicate.messagePlaceholder: e.g. Please read the updated policy before the team meeting.
communicate.sent: {{ count }} people were asked to read and confirm.
communicate.sentOne: 1 person was asked to read and confirm.
communicate.sentWithSkipped: {{ count }} were asked to read and confirm. {{ skipped }} had already been asked.
communicate.alreadyAsked: All {{ count }} had already been asked to confirm this version.

ai.draftHint: Uses the organisation profile. Read the draft before you save.
ai.suggestHint: The suggestions are based on the organisation profile. Pick one to fill in the form.

prompts.summarise: Summarise {{ type }} {{ code }} “{{ title }}” in a few sentences for the management review.
prompts.explain: Explain in plain words what {{ type }} {{ code }} “{{ title }}” is, which requirements of the standards it documents, and what an auditor looks for.
prompts.scopeExclusions: Which requirements can a scope statement exclude, and how should the justification be written?
prompts.obligation: When is a requirement from an interested party a legal or other obligation the organisation must record?
prompts.policyContent: What must a policy contain to meet clause 5.2, and how do I write it simply and clearly?
prompts.raci: How do I assign R, A, C and I on a responsibility, and what are common mistakes?

improve.analysis: Review context analysis {{ code }} “{{ title }}”. Which important internal or external issues are missing, and which factors are unclear?
improve.party: Review interested party {{ code }} “{{ title }}”. Are the needs and expectations complete, and which of them are legal or other obligations?
improve.scope: Review scope statement {{ code }} “{{ title }}”. Are the boundaries, sites and exclusions clear and justified?
improve.policy: Review policy {{ code }} “{{ title }}” against clause 5.2. Does it contain the required commitments, and does it suit our purpose?
improve.responsibility: Review responsibility {{ code }} “{{ title }}”. Is exactly one person accountable, and is the authority clear?

reviewOverdue.title: Review {{ code }} “{{ title }}”
reviewOverdue.why: The review is overdue. Auditors check that context, policies and responsibilities are kept up to date.

policyNotCommunicated.title: Communicate policy {{ code }} “{{ title }}”
policyNotCommunicated.why: The policy is approved, but nobody has been asked to read and confirm it yet.

notices.submit: {{ code }} has been sent for approval.
notices.return: {{ code }} has been returned to draft.
notices.review: {{ code }} has been marked as reviewed.

errors.module_disabled: Context and leadership is switched off for the organisation.
errors.record_retired: A retired item can no longer be edited.
errors.change_reason_required: Say why the approved content is changing.
errors.invalid_status: This step is not possible in the item's current status. Reload the page and try again.
errors.invalid_category: One of the factors has a category that does not belong to this method.
errors.invalid_owner: The owner must be a member of the organisation.
errors.invalid_owner_filter: The owner filter is not valid.
errors.multiple_accountable: Only one can be accountable for the result (A).
errors.duplicate_assignment: Each person, role or department can only appear once.
errors.invalid_assignee: The person, role or department does not exist in the organisation.
errors.not_controlled: This type has no approval steps.
errors.invalid_clause: One of the clauses does not exist in the standard. Choose it from the list.
errors.no_recipients: Nobody holds this role or is in the department. Choose people, or add people to the role first.
errors.forbidden: You do not have access to do this.
errors.not_found: The item (or a linked document) was not found.
errors.validation: Some values are not valid. Check the form and try again.
